general:
Thrive Messenger Help

Thrive Messenger supports multi-server chat, accessible keyboard workflows, and admin tooling from one client. Press F1 in any window for context help. Press Escape or Command+W to close help and return.

Use the menu bar or context menus for all major actions: contacts, chats, file transfers, server management, bot rules, and updates.
login:
Login and Server Selection

Choose a server from the Server list, then enter username and password to sign in. Use Manage Servers to add, edit, remove, and set a primary server entry.

Server host entries support both standard DNS names and Web3-style domains (including Freename/ENS/Unstoppable-style names).

Auto-login uses saved credentials and the selected server profile. If login fails, confirm server host/port/TLS values in Administration settings.
main:
Contacts Window

The main window provides contacts, search, status controls, user directory, server info, server manager, settings, and updates. Context menus and menu actions mirror button actions for keyboard-first use.

  • Start Chat: Return or menu action
  • Send File: Alt+F or menu action
  • User Directory: browse and filter users across configured servers
  • File Transfers: view sent/received files and saved locations
chat:
Chat Window

Default key behavior is Enter to send, Command+Enter for new line, and Control+Enter to send a file. Enter action can be changed in Settings.

Chat history is keyboard-navigable and can be logged based on global and per-contact rules. Typing indicators and message readout are configurable for accessibility. With Announce typing start/stop on, you hear when someone starts typing to you once, even if their chat window isn't open, and when they stop without sending. Announcements go straight to NVDA when it is running.

In chat history, press Enter on a message with no link to open the full message in a read-only text box you can read line by line; Escape closes it. Links are covered below. The context menu (Applications key or Shift+F10) also has View Full Message and Copy Message. Control+C on a message copies it to the clipboard and says Copied. Edit Message only appears on your own recent messages (admins can edit any message); press Enter to save the edit or Escape to cancel. Delete Message (or the Delete key) removes a message for both people when you sent it or are an admin, after you confirm. Settings has Delete messages for everyone (on by default) and Also delete attached files when deleting a message, which moves files you received to the Recycle Bin.

Chat tabs

Chats open in their own Chats window and the contact list stays open. Each conversation is a tab: Ctrl+Tab and Ctrl+Shift+Tab switch, Ctrl+1 to Ctrl+9 jump (Ctrl+9 is the last), Ctrl+W or Ctrl+F4 closes a tab, and Ctrl+0 goes to the contact list. New messages never switch tabs or move focus; the tab shows an unread count. Turn tabs off, or return to the older window behaviour, in Settings, General, Chat Behavior.

Inside a conversation

Ctrl+Page Down and Ctrl+Page Up move between Messages, Chat Archive and File Transfers. Chat Archive (formerly Saved Messages) lists saved days by year and month; Enter reads a day as read-only text and Escape goes back. Ctrl+S on a message saves it there. File Transfers lists every file and voice message with this person; Get Again asks their app for a file that is no longer on this device.

Emoji

Ctrl+E opens Insert Emoji: type part of a name, arrow to it, press Enter to insert it at the cursor.

Voice messages and voicemail

Ctrl+R records a voice message; press it again to stop, then Send, Play Back or Discard. Ctrl+Shift+R leaves a voicemail, which waits on the server for people who are offline. On a voice message, Enter plays or stops, Space pauses, and Left or Right skips 5 seconds. File, Voicemail lists voicemail you received. Live voice calls are still switched off.

On a Mac

Use Command where Windows uses Control. Switch conversation tabs with Control+Tab or Command+Shift+] and [. Switch inner tabs with Control+Page Down and Up, or Command+Option+Right and Left. Delete a message with Command+Delete. Announcements go to VoiceOver when it is on.

Message history

Opening a chat shows the last 200 messages from the server, on every device and after restarting, in order and without duplicates. Load earlier messages (or Up Arrow on the first message) shows older ones; the Chat Archive tab lists every day of the conversation. Focus goes to the message box and the backlog is not read out. Settings, General, Chat Behavior has Start chats fresh each time; nothing is deleted when it is on.

Read receipts

Your messages end with sent, delivered, or read and the time. You hear Read by, once, when your newest message is read. A message you receive counts as read after it stays selected for 2 seconds (1 to 10 in Settings) or when it is the newest one in the open chat. Settings, General, Chat Behavior: Send read receipts (on by default); turning it off hides yours and theirs.

Links in chats

A message with links says how many at the end, for example 3 links. Right Arrow and Left Arrow move between a message's links and read link 2 of 3 and the page title; Up and Down still move between messages. Enter or Space opens the link you moved to. With one link Enter opens it, and with several Enter shows a list. Double-click also opens links, and View Full Message shows them as real clickable links.

Full view shows the whole page inside Thrive, with Back, Forward, Reload, Open in default browser and Close. Escape or Control+W (Command+W on a Mac) returns to the message the link came from. Alt+Left and Alt+Right go back and forward, and F5 reloads.

The message context menu has a Links group below the usual options: open or copy a link or its title; Show list of links in this message, this conversation, this chat window or all conversations; and Remove links (this link, all in this message, a link you pick in this conversation, all in this conversation, or all in all conversations). In a link list, each item reads title, address, sender and time. Enter opens it, Control+C copies the link, Control+Shift+C copies the title, Delete removes it, and the Applications key shows more. Links in your own messages are removed for everyone, since only the sender or an admin can do that. Links other people sent are hidden on this device only. Thrive asks before either.

The server looks up page titles in the background, never visiting private network addresses, and the address is used when there is no title. Settings, Chat Behavior: Open links in (Full view inside Thrive, Default browser, Ask each time), Fetch link titles, and Sort link lists (Newest first or By sender).

Getting around long histories

The message context menu has Links in this message (a submenu per link, by title and address, to open or copy it), Link lists and removal, and Go to (also Control+G). Go to lists Messages with links, Messages from a person, My messages, Unread messages, By date and Search; each item reads sender, time and first words, and Enter goes to the message, loading older history first when needed. Alt+Left goes back to where you were. Alt+Down and Alt+Up go to the next or previous message with a link. Control+Home and Control+End go to the first and last message.

Chat rooms

The Groups tab is the room directory with search. Enter opens a room as a chat tab (joining a public room first). Create room sets a name, topic, description, public or private, and expiry. Rooms and history are kept on the server. In a room, @mention someone to notify them. Your messages say sent, read by 2 of 5, or read by everyone. The Members tab (Control+Page Down) has the topic and members, with their role, whether they're muted and whether they've read the newest message; the Applications key on a member offers direct message, mention, change role, mute, remove and ban. Roles are owner, admin, moderator, member and guest. Agents answer in the room when @mentioned and never answer each other. Settings has Room messages when the room isn't open: mentions only, every message, or nothing.
directory:
User Directory

Directory shows Everyone, Online, Offline, and Admins tabs with sort/filter options and server labels. Duplicate usernames across servers are displayed as separate entries.

If cross-server directory messaging is enabled in Administration settings, you can start a direct message to users on configured remote servers. When duplicates exist, the client lets you choose the target server user and remembers that default until you choose another.
admin:
Administration

Server Side Commands supports command-based administration such as alerts, account actions, and scheduled restart. Command responses are stored in an accessible history list for arrow-key review.

Administration also provides bot rules management and server/update configuration. Unauthorized actions return explicit server-side errors.

In the command text box, type ? or help (with or without a leading slash) to see command usage help.
settings:
Settings

Settings are split into General, Audio, and Administration tabs. Configure sound packs, volume, accessibility behavior, chat key behavior, and layout preferences.

Account controls include changing your password and permanently deleting your account from the connected server. Account deletion requires typing your username and confirming a final warning. It revokes Thrive credentials and unlinks connected identities without deleting external Mastodon or WordPress accounts.

Administration settings include server host/port/TLS, update feed/repo fallback, restart scheduling, and toggle for cross-server directory direct messaging. Server host supports Web3-style domains as well as standard DNS hostnames.
server_info:
Server Info

Server Info reports active server name, host, port, encryption state, online users/admins, uptime, and file policy limits.

Use this view for quick diagnostics to confirm the active connection and server policy before troubleshooting.
bot_rules:
Bot Rules Manager

Bot Rules Manager supports load, edit, save, and reset per bot. Global baseline rules can come from an agent ZIP/file ruleset, and admin overrides are stored per admin scope.

Admins can edit and reset rules. Non-admin users can request and view active rules in read-only mode.
